answer: 542 of 4623 blocks that publish a bar count also publish an annualised figure, and all 542 of those re-derive to within 5e-04 of the figure printed, with an implied bars-per-year constant of 241.1972..243.1078 (median 241.9971); downstream, 6 of 24 reader modules divide a published count, 0 multiply it and 5 annualise it (scripts/etf_book_forward.py, scripts/trial_labor_w17.py, scripts/trial_labor_w18.py, scripts/trial_labor_w19.py, scripts/trial_labor_w20.py, scripts/trial_labor_w21.py); 542 of the 542 annualised blocks publish a count and nothing that could reveal a duplicated row

excluded_modules.reason: this study -- its own selftest literals name faces

limits: a bar count is recognised only as an integer under bars, n_bars, bar_count, n_bar, bars_observed or as a len() over something that mentions bars; a bare payload["bars"] read cannot be told apart from a read of the bar LIST (the forward ledger stores a list under the same name), so it is not credited as a count read here -- this census is a lower bound
roles are decided line-level on the module's own literals: a count that travels through several helper frames before being divided is invisible

a reader is attributed to a face only when its own literal states the face path; a module that reaches the face through a constant defined elsewhere is counted in reader_modules_basename_only or not at all

the annualisation arm re-derives cagr from (total_ret, years) and compares with the published cagr at 5e-04; a face that annualises with a different formula (log return, arithmetic mean x bars) would read as not re-deriving, which is a statement about the formula and not about the count
lists are walked 40 elements deep at 4 levels; a count inside a longer tail is not seen
faces above 1000000 bytes are published as too_big rather than parsed
